benchmark.category: a single-file browser open-world campus game with daily missions, drivable vehicles and a day/night cycle
benchmark.users: casual players and demo judges playing short sessions on a phone or desktop browser

requirements.source_phrase: Count bystanders, match the oval ring and let players re-ask people who wander back in
requirements.statement: In the Crowd Control mission the HUD's remaining-people count rises when a bystander who was not in the original crowd walks into the oval on the ground, falls only once a person has physically walked out of that oval, and the success card appears only when the oval is empty
requirements.notes: Amended for the new window: the count now has to include bystanders and match the drawn oval, not only the original crowd, so the inherited 'count falls only when a person leaves' wording was too narrow. Surface is the '/* 9. CROWD CONTROL */' block (mxCrowdIn) in /app/frontend/public/game/index.html; read the HUD count and the NPC positions from page.evaluate rather than the mission's own flag.

requirements.source_phrase: Count bystanders, match the oval ring and let players re-ask people who wander back in
requirements.statement: mxCrowdIn counts every frame the standing NPCs whose position lies inside the Crowd Control ellipse the mission draws on the ground (half-width m.r=105, half-height 0.45*m.r) — bystanders who walked in included, anyone knocked down or holding another mission's role excluded — and mxFinish fires only when that count reaches zero, so a person outside the drawn ring is never counted and a person inside it is never missed
requirements.notes: Amended because the previous wording counted knocked-down people and keyed the count to a circle whose radius differed from the ring drawn on screen; the features the user asked for define the count as standing people inside the drawn oval. Check with a person standing just inside and just outside the ellipse edge, and with a bystander walking in from outside.

requirements.source_phrase: Give campus buggies headlights and tail lights so night drives feel complete
requirements.statement: On the campus play screen at night (game clock 21:00) driving a campus buggy shows a headlight beam falling on the road ahead of it and red tail lights behind it while the buggy moves
requirements.notes: The user's buggy line; the agent's report and the 'campus buggies get no headlights' open item are both unverified. Reach it with S.t=1260, enter a buggy and drive; compare the same shot at 10:00.

requirements.source_phrase: Give campus buggies headlights and tail lights so night drives feel complete
requirements.statement: The served night pass draws a beam sprite ahead of the player's driven buggy along its heading and red tail lights behind it every frame, with the buggy handled by the same branch that lights the other vehicle kinds the player can drive
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: the 'NIGHT LIGHTING' block (drawNightLights) in /app/frontend/public/game/index.html. A buggy branch missing from the player's-vehicle draw is the likely gap, since the earlier pass lit only the main-road traffic and some vehicle kinds.
